title: Multicenter registry study on proton radiotherapy of mediastinal lymphoma
summary:
Improvements in multimodal therapy have led to high curation rates in lymphoma patients. In addition, these cancer entities (Hodgkin's lymphoma and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma) often affect very young patients. Due to the high healing rates, the long-term effects of therapy are increasingly important: more than 40% of patients suffer from chronic, therapy-associated sequelae 30 years after successful therapy. For this reason, an important focus of current research is the reduction of therapy-associated toxicity. A certain trend of dose reduction and reduction of irradiation fields are the results of research of the last decades. Another interesting approach to protecting adjacent organs is the use of modern radiation techniques, such as particle radiation therapy with protons.

This prospective registry study on proton radiotherapy for mediastinal lymphoma aims to capture the frequency, feasibility, and adverse effects after protons in this patient population. These data should then serve as a basis for concrete therapy recommendations and assessment of side effects. Close cooperation with the study groups should also allow a comparative analysis to comparable patients who were not treated with protons at a later date.

Since this is a registry study, there is no difference to the standard treatment for therapy and follow-up. Additional study-related effort is created for the patient by completing quality of life questionnaires.

interventions.name: Radiotherapy by means of protons in mediastinal lymphomas. Irradiation dose and sparing of organs at risk should be performed according to current guidelines or trials.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- histologically confirmed lymphoma according to WHO
- informed consent 
- age ≥ 18 years
- Existence of the need for mediastinal radiotherapy and suspected benefit of mediastinal radiotherapy by protons compared to photon irradiation (e.g., improved sparing of heart, lungs and/or mamma compared to photon irradiation)
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years

- Non-consent of the patient to share his data

- Revocation of the patient for study participation
